niche: online spiritual and shadow work courses
prompt_text: What are the best online courses for learning shadow work and spiritual practice?
answer_verbatim:
“Best” depends on whether you want a Jungian, Buddhist, or theistic approach. These are promising options from the available listings:

### Shadow work
- **[Engage the Shadow — Jung Platform](https://jungplatform.com/course/engage-the-shadow)** — A broad introduction featuring ten depth-psychology teachers, with video and audio lessons and practical exercises. A good starting point if you want several perspectives.
- **[Encounters with the Shadow — Jung Platform](https://jungplatform.com/course/encounters-with-the-shadow)** — A more focused Jungian course taught by analyst and author James Hollis. Consider it if you want a structured introduction grounded in Jungian psychology.
- **[Diving into the Shadow — Michael Lennox](https://michaellennox.com/classes/shadow/)** — A four-week online course; potentially a good fit if you prefer a shorter, time-bounded program.
- **[Shadow Work for Conscious Relationships — Jung Center of Chicago](https://jungchicago.org/product/shadow-work-for-conscious-relationships/)** — A relationship-focused option featuring Connie Zweig, a Jungian-oriented therapist and author.

### Spiritual practice
- **[Naropa University’s online learning courses](https://www.naropa.edu/academics/personal-enrichment/)** — Includes a free introductory mindfulness course and longer Buddhist study-and-practice series. A strong choice for a Buddhist-informed approach.
- **[Contemplative Living I — Center for Theology and the Sciences](https://ctsnet.edu/events/contemplative-living-i-contemplative-practices-in-daily-life/)** — A four-month online, experiential course centered on Christian contemplative practice.
- **[Closer Than Breath](https://closerthanbreath.com/)** — Offers a self-paced course in Centering Prayer, with an interfaith framing.

**My quick picks:** Start with *Engage the Shadow* for a broad shadow-work overview, and Naropa’s free mindfulness course for a low-commitment spiritual-practice introduction. If you want a more personal or intensive experience, check whether a course includes live discussion, instructor feedback, or community support.

Course schedules, prices, and availability can change, so confirm those on the provider’s site. Shadow work can bring up difficult emotions; choose a course that encourages pacing and support, and consider working with a qualified mental-health professional if you’re dealing with trauma or significant distress.
